The 45.9% valuation gap and 7.89% yield offer a margin of safety while the desk waits for the pullback to resolve.

bear_case.thesis: EFERT is in a confirmed downtrend below both its SMA20 and SMA50 with weak momentum, and the same-day filing shows a 32% YoY profit drop reported with internally conflicting EPS figures. The 'undervalued' verdict rests on a composite fair value that masks a 5.6x spread between its own methods, making the safety margin far less solid than it looks.
pillars: Price 190.14 is below SMA20 (192.37) and SMA50 (196.86), 20-day return -4.36%, RSI14 43.4 (sub-50), TA memo momentum 'flat' and stance 'cautious'
2QCY26 net profit down 32% YoY to Rs3.8bn, news impact rated 4 (material) and dated same-day (2026-07-31)
The filing itself carries conflicting EPS figures for the same quarter (Rs2.85 vs Rs2.33) — an internal data-quality gap, not just a bear narrative
Fair-value composite (277.34) hides massive method dispersion: earnings-power 101.59 vs DDM 572.58, a 5.6x spread, per FA memo 'directionally suggestive rather than precise'
Payout ratio already high at 76.87%; FA memo notes dividend sustainability 'depends on whether the recent quarterly profit decline persists', and no support level is defined (levels.support: null)
bear_case.attack_on_bull: The bull's valuation pillar (277.34 fair value, 45.9% undervalued) is the weakest: it is a composite of four methods that disagree by 5.6x (101.59 to 572.58), and its earnings inputs (EPS 15.94, growth_est 30%) predate or may not yet reflect the just-reported 32% YoY quarterly profit decline. A composite average across wildly divergent models is not a precise floor — it is a number that moves a lot once the input earnings figure gets restated.
bear_case.broker_challenge: The one source document is a filing digest, not a broker call, and it fails its own internal consistency check — reporting two different EPS figures (Rs2.85 vs Rs2.33) for the same quarter. Per the owner principle, this is exactly the kind of number that must be treated as unverified in magnitude even if directionally right; any valuation or dividend-coverage conclusion drawn from it before reconciliation is provisional.
bear_case.worst_case: If the quarterly profit decline persists at anywhere near the reported 32% YoY pace, payout coverage on the 76.87% ratio could tighten, pressuring the 7.89% yield the bull leans on; technically, with price already -4.36% over 20 days and no defined support level in the TA memo, a break below SMA50 (196.86) — already the case — has no stated floor to arrest further downside.
